challengeFindings.title: A test whose child traps or ignores SIGTERM (the `scripts/ci/bkit-machine-lock.sh run` owner, or `sh -c "trap '' TERM; ..."`) still blocks the worker for the child's full run, because the injected limit only sends the default SIGTERM

A test that uses most of its budget, followed by a file-level or `describe`-level `afterEach` that cleans up with `execFileSync` (for example `git worktree remove`), has the cleanup killed after a few ms; the passing test is reported failed and the cleanup is skipped

A hung `execSync` or `spawnSync` that the wrapper stops throws a bare `Error`, so a caller or test that reads `error.stdout`, `error.stderr` or `error.status` to show what the child printed before it hung gets `undefined`
A test declared with `{ timeout: Infinity }` (a Vitest-supported value) makes every child call it runs throw `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` ("must be an unsigned integer. Received Infinity") instead of running

A developer shell that exports `CI=false` or `CI=0` gets the strict 30s bats limit from `tests/shell/setup_suite.bash`, while `vitest.timeout-budget.ts` (`env.CI === "true" || env.CI === "1"`) treats the same shell as local and scales the other runners, so bats tests under load fail on `timeout after` alone

The skill lock drops its integrity hash for find-skills, so a changed or tampered upstream copy of that agent-read skill can no longer be detected, and the next setup check re-fetches it from an unpinned upstream

challengeFindings.title: A test that mocks the clock (`vi.setSystemTime`, or `vi.useFakeTimers` with `Date` faked) moves the child limit with it: a future time kills every child call in the test body at 1 ms, so a passing test fails with `did not finish within 1 ms`, and a past time removes the limit, so a hung child blocks the worker for its full run

A `beforeAll(fn, 60_000)` (or any hook given its own longer timeout) whose setup child takes longer than the file's default hook timeout has that child killed at the default, so the hook fails and every test in the file is skipped, with an error that blames "the running test's remaining time" when no test is running
